newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM says he agrees with FinMin on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM says he agrees with FinMin on EMU.

text.p: Sweden's Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Thursday that he and Finance Minister Erik Asbrink had the same view on membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
"We are in accord (on EMU)," Persson told reporters after a speech at mortgage lender Landshypotek's annual meeting.
"It has almost been a bit boring because we have had the same view all along," he said.
Early on Thursday Social Democratic parliament member Bengt-Ola Ryttar told a TV4 news show that Persson was negative to an EMU link while Asbrink was more positive.
When asked if he was negative to EMU, Persson told Reuters: "No, that's not right."
"I have the same view as I've had all along," Persson said. "From an economic point of view it is easy to see the advantages. From a broader political angle you have to look at the whole picture."
"The party board will soon announce its decision," he said.
The ruling Social Democrats have previously said they will announce the party's view on EMU in May or June.
